value: This article explores Robert Nozick's proposed solution to the challenges of voluntary charitable giving, such as the free-rider problem and fear of exploitation. While acknowledging the appeal of compulsory redistribution for overcoming these issues, Nozick rejects it as a violation of individual rights. Instead, he proposes a voluntary mechanism where individuals contract to give contingent upon others' contributions. This concept, formalized by Alex Tabarrok as a "dominant assurance contract," functions like crowdfunding: donations are collected only if a set threshold is met, otherwise returned. This mechanism offers a viable and ethical approach to public good provision, with crowdfunding serving as a successful real-world application.
